paragraphs.title: The Friends’ Words Bring No Comfort

answers: Many such things
Good news
His friends’ prayers

easy.q: What does Job say he has already heard?

answers: Teachers of righteousness
Miserable comforters
Faithful witnesses
easy.q: What does Job call his friends?

Only silence
Only his friends’ words

easy.q: How does Job feel about God and his enemies?

answers: A place of rest
A mark or target
A judge before his friends

answers: His great strength
His gauntness and weakness
His happiness
medium.explanation: Job’s leanness refers to his wasted, weakened condition.
medium.q: What does “my leanness” describe in this passage?

From comfort to joy and rest

medium.explanation: The passage moves through increasingly violent images: surrounding, tearing, striking, breaking, and targeting.

That he is hiding from danger
That he is escaping his enemies
challenge.explanation: A mark is something aimed at, emphasizing Job’s sense of deliberate and ongoing assault.

That the suffering is a continuing sequence of harsh attacks
That Job is mainly describing comfort

challenge.q: What do the many violent verbs in this passage convey?

answers: Royal garments
Sackcloth
Festive clothing
easy.explanation: Job says, “I have sewed sackcloth upon my skin.”
easy.q: What did Job sew upon his skin?

answers: His horn
His friends’ clothing
The ground
easy.explanation: He says, “I have … defiled my horn in the dust.”
easy.q: What did Job defile in the dust?

answers: His hands were full of injustice
There was no injustice in his hands and his prayer was pure
He did not pray at all
easy.explanation: Job says, “Not for any injustice in mine hands: also my prayer is pure.”
easy.q: What does Job say about his hands and prayer?
